title: Sicilian Eggplant Pasta
subtitle: with Green Olives and Parmesan
description: Rustic, tomato-based sauces are the hallmark of Sicilian cooking. Here, we pan-fry eggplant until soft and silky, then add tomatoes, just-tender pasta and a handful of olives. To finish? Sprinkle with plenty of parmesan, of course!

steps.text: Prep ingredients: Bring a medium saucepan of salted water to the boil for the pasta. Thinly slice the onion. Cut the eggplant into 2cm chunks (see Kitchen 101). Quarter the olives. Crush or finely chop 2 garlic cloves. Finely grate the parmesan.
Cook pasta: Cook three-quarters of the pasta in the pan of boiling water for 12 mins or until al dente. Reserve 160ml (⅔ cup) cooking water, then drain the pasta.

Soften veggies: Meanwhile, heat 1 tbs olive oil in a medium deep frypan over medium heat. Cook the onion, stirring occasionally, for 3-4 mins until softened. Add the eggplant and cook, stirring occasionally, for 3-4 mins until tender. Season with salt and pepper. Add the garlic, Tuscan seasoning and 2 tbs tomato paste and cook, stirring, for 30 secs.

Simmer sauce: Add the tomatoes, reserved cooking water and ½ tsp sugar to the veggie mixture and bring to the boil. Reduce the heat to medium and cook, stirring occasionally, for 10-12 mins until thickened.
Serve up: Stir the pasta, olives and half the parmesan into the sauce. Taste, then season with salt and pepper. Divide the pasta among bowls, scatter over the remaining parmesan and enjoy!

Kitchen 101: Only 300g (3½ cups) eggplant is needed for this recipe, so if your eggplant looks very large, you may want to check this. Either weigh it or fill a measuring jug with the chopped eggplant for a quick way to measure.
